| What contribution should the board and executives each provide? | [CGOV.4 - Design Board and Executive Contributions](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov4---design-board-and-executive-contributions) | A design for the needed work and its result exchanges under the corporate powers. |
| Do we need a committee, and can its findings be used? | [CGOV.5 - Choose an Arrangement for Independent Corporate Oversight, with or without a Committee](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov5---choose-an-arrangement-for-independent-corporate-oversight-with-or-without-a-committee) | A design for a permitted oversight arrangement, with its remit, participants, support and receiving use. |
| Does a director's or owner's interest affect this matter? | [CGOV.6 - Expose Conflicts and Related-Party Interests](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov6---expose-conflicts-and-related-party-interests) | The relevant interest, conflict conditions and required safeguards. |
| What independent review or participation arrangement is needed? | [CGOV.7 - Arrange Independent Review and a Disinterested Corporate Decision](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov7---arrange-independent-review-and-a-disinterested-corporate-decision) | Usable review findings and an eligible decision arrangement, retaining the separate corporate act. |
| What information is owed, to whom and when? | [CGOV.8 - Provide Corporate Information under Applicable Rights and Duties](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov8---provide-corporate-information-under-applicable-rights-and-duties) | Required content provided through usable access, with confidentiality requirements and the limits of specialist conclusions preserved. |
| Will the proposed control actually operate in the work? | [CGOV.9 - Establish and Operate Internal Control](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov9---establish-and-operate-internal-control) | A control and the means to operate it, with supported effectiveness and its limits kept distinct. |
| What can this audit or assurance conclusion support? | [CGOV.10 - Obtain and Use a Scoped Audit or Assurance Conclusion for Corporate Governance](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov10---obtain-and-use-a-scoped-audit-or-assurance-conclusion-for-corporate-governance) | A contribution qualified by its subject, criteria, period, provider and limitations. |
| Has the corporate decision been made, or only described? | [CGOV.11 - Make and Record a Corporate Decision](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov11---make-and-record-a-corporate-decision) | The act performed through the applicable procedure and its proper record, with remaining conditions clear. |
| How can a minority holder protect or exercise a right? | [CGOV.12 - Protect Corporate Minority Holders' Rights and Enable Contest or Exit](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov12---protect-corporate-minority-holders-rights-and-enable-contest-or-exit) | A timely use of an available protection, exercise, contest or exit route under its actual conditions. |
| What response should follow a performance exception? | [CGOV.13 - Monitor Corporate Performance and Require an Account](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov13---monitor-corporate-performance-and-require-an-account) | An account against the undertaking, an authorized response and follow-up on its consequence. |
| Should a governing instrument or arrangement change, and how? | [CGOV.14 - Decide Whether and How to Change Corporate Governing Instruments and Arrangements](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov14---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-corporate-governing-instruments-and-arrangements) | A supported decision to retain the arrangement or repair its operation, or a revision made effective through the current amendment powers and required acts, with implementation addressed. |
| Should we reuse, adapt or replace a way of doing governance work? | [CGOV.15 - Decide Whether and How to Change Corporate-Governance Methods](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov15---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-corporate-governance-methods) | A compared method choice, retained or changed within the available powers, directed at the working difficulty. |
| Why does a correct local action fail to constitute the larger work? | [CGOV.16 - Reconcile Constituent and Encompassing Corporate Governance Work](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov16---reconcile-constituent-and-encompassing-corporate-governance-work) | How the larger work is performed through its constituent actions, and a correction to an action, its conditions or the explanation of that connection. |
| How can useful governance methods remain obtainable across succession? | [CGOV.17 - Deliberately Continue and Change Corporate-Governance Culture](CORPORATE-GOVERNANCE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#cgov17---deliberately-continue-and-change-corporate-governance-culture) | The learning, access, assistance or practice change needed for receiving work, with actual use and retention distinguished. |

A financial recommendation can inform the authorized participants' judgement; its valuation does not confer the power to commit the corporation. Use CGOV.3 when that power is unresolved and CGOV.11 when the assignment includes making the act. An adequate existing delegation can permit ordinary action without another board decision. Keep the recommendation's material assumptions in the receiving decision.

Putting a corporate decision into effect may still require resources and support. Use [OPS.11](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops11---coordinate-interacting-operating-structures) for unresolved dependencies among operating contributions. Use [ADM.9](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm9---provide-a-usable-administrative-result) when a required administrative condition, such as permitted access, is not yet usable. Allocating cases within existing responsibilities and powers remains an operating question. A change to organizational responsibilities or decision rights calls for the appropriate organizational change; neither additional participants nor a new case alone implies that change.


### Engineering.Reference:1.24 - Fulfil an administrative request and improve its handling

| Your question | Start with | First useful result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What work should this request enable? | [ADM.1 - Frame the Administrative Condition Needed for the Work](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm1---frame-the-administrative-condition-needed-for-the-work) | The administrative condition to provide, its recipient and its provider, distinguished from the work it enables. |
| Who participates, receives, owes or decides? | [ADM.2 - Establish the Relevant Participants and Relations for an Administrative Action](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm2---establish-the-relevant-participants-and-relations-for-an-administrative-action) | The relevant participants and their relations, or the institutional fact still needed to identify them. |
| What changed, and when does it take effect? | [ADM.3 - Determine What Changed in Administrative Relations and When It Takes Effect](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm3---determine-what-changed-in-administrative-relations-and-when-it-takes-effect) | The condition applicable at the requested time, distinguishing its effective date from recording or correction when that affects the decision. |
| Do these participant accounts concern the same thing? | [ADM.4 - Reconcile Participant-Relative Administrative Accounts](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm4---reconcile-participant-relative-administrative-accounts) | A correspondence that preserves each participant's meaning, or an identified disagreement about the object or claim. |
| How should this repeated case be handled? | [ADM.5 - Design Reusable Instructions for Administrative Requests](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm5---design-reusable-instructions-for-administrative-requests) | A reusable handling instruction covering provision, correction, refusal and exceptions. |
| How can this exceptional or blocked case continue? | [ADM.6 - Resolve an Administrative Exception](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm6---resolve-an-administrative-exception) | A usable continuation or a reasoned refusal with its correction or challenge route; an unresolved case identifies the question and who can answer it. |
| What must be established for this decision? | [ADM.7 - Check the Claim Needed for This Administrative Decision](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm7---check-the-claim-needed-for-this-administrative-decision) | An answer supported by evidence, or the evidence or qualified check still needed to answer the claim question. |
| Does this action have the required permission? | [ADM.8 - Establish and Exercise the Required Permission for an Administrative Action](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm8---establish-and-exercise-the-required-permission-for-an-administrative-action) | The permission and conditions that apply, an established absence of permission, or the unresolved question about authority. |
| How do we turn approval into a usable result? | [ADM.9 - Provide a Usable Administrative Result](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm9---provide-a-usable-administrative-result) | Provision the recipient can use; if provision is still unsuccessful or uncertain, the next action and who takes it. |
| Do the obligation, performance and records agree? | [ADM.10 - Reconcile Administrative Obligations, Performance and Records](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm10---reconcile-administrative-obligations-performance-and-records) | An account of what was owed, fulfilled and recorded, with any needed correction identified. |
| How do providers deliver one administrative result? | [ADM.11 - Join Providers Around the Administrative Result](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm11---join-providers-around-the-administrative-result) | Connected provider contributions, the conditions each receiver needs and responsibility for recovery when a join fails. |
| Will these records support the uses that matter? | [ADM.13 - Keep Administrative Records Fit for Their Uses](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm13---keep-administrative-records-fit-for-their-uses) | Records retaining the identity, context and correction history needed for authorized retrieval under applicable retention rules. |
| What purpose does this control serve, and who may decide about it? | [ADM.14 - Connect an Administrative Control to Its Purpose and Competent Decision](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm14---connect-an-administrative-control-to-its-purpose-and-competent-decision) | The protected interest, applicable rule and responsible authority for interpretation, exception, remedy or change. |
| What did the arrangement achieve, and at whose burden? | [ADM.15 - Judge Administrative Consequences](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm15---judge-administrative-consequences) | An assessment including usable provision, refusals, unfinished or excluded cases, time and effort shifted to others. |
| How can the arrangement change while open cases continue? | [ADM.16 - Decide Whether and How to Change an Administrative Arrangement Without Losing Open Cases](ORGANIZATION-ADMINISTRATION-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#adm16---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-an-administrative-arrangement-without-losing-open-cases) | A decision to retain the arrangement, an authorized transition preserving applicable terms for open cases, or a change proposal for the responsible decision maker. |

Start with ADM for the permission, organizational condition or provision that enables someone's work. [Operations Management](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) helps with queues, capacity and competing work. For example, an administrator can establish a person's access while the operation still needs to schedule the work that access permits.

When participant accounts cannot be reconciled because their meanings or object boundaries differ, [SIE.4-SIE.6](SEMANTIC-INTEGRATION-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#sie4---judge-cross-source-correspondences-and-their-permitted-uses) supply the needed semantic work. ADM.4 and ADM.10 apply the resulting distinctions to administrative provision and obligations. A disputed assignment can require [Organization Change Engineering](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md).

Use [SYSE.24](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse24---choose-how-the-project-will-obtain-a-needed-engineering-result) to compare complete ways to obtain an administrative result; ADM.2, ADM.3, ADM.11 and ADM.14 supply the relevant institutional conditions. For the supporting platform, use SYSE.26 to design the user/provider interaction, SYSE.28 to place a control where it can check or enforce the relevant rule, and SYSE.29 for technical migration or retirement. ADM.16 contains the administrative instruction for changing case handling; use [Method Engineering](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) when the reusable method or its variants need development.


### Engineering.Reference:1.25 - Maintain equipment and manage maintenance

An alarm, delayed repair or fleet result can lead to different questions. Open the Method for the result you need now, using evidence that is already adequate for it. The [six ordinary maintenance entries](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#practical-entries) offer direct starts; the [full pattern index](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) remains available when none fits.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which equipment, actual configuration and required use does the maintenance question concern? | [MNT.1 - Identify the Maintained System, Use, and Permission Boundary](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt1---identify-the-maintained-system-use-and-permission-boundary) | A bounded maintained System and use, with the operating and permission conditions that change the answer. |
| Should we keep the current maintenance policy or choose another task? | [MNT.2 - Select and Reopen the Maintenance Policy](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt2---select-and-reopen-the-maintenance-policy) | An applicable retain or change decision for the failure and use. Keeping a policy requires an adequate basis, not merely an unproved alternative. |
| What can this failure history tell us? | [MNT.3 - Establish Degradation and Failure Evidence for Maintenance](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt3---establish-degradation-and-failure-evidence-for-maintenance) | A qualified failure account that distinguishes events, exposure, mechanism and cause without claiming more than the evidence supports. |
| Does this alarm or trend show a changed condition under the actual load and speed? | [MNT.4 - Monitor and Interpret System Condition for Maintenance](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt4---monitor-and-interpret-system-condition-for-maintenance) | A condition interpretation with its measurement and comparison limits. It need not predict remaining life or select a repair. |
| Are the spare, tools, competence and support suitable and available for the selected task? | [MNT.5 - Prepare Maintenance Service Capability, Spares, Tools, and Authority](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt5---prepare-maintenance-service-capability-spares-tools-and-authority) | Task-specific readiness or the exact missing contribution. Missing spare applicability can prevent replacement without defeating a sufficient recommendation. |
| What maintenance response can we recommend now? | [MNT.6 - Diagnose Condition and Choose a Maintenance Response](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt6---diagnose-condition-and-choose-a-maintenance-response) | A supported recommendation or selected intervention from the plausible responses. Finish sufficient advice; investigate or perform physical work only when that further result is needed. |
| Will the whole intervention fit the operating commitment? | [MNT.7 - Coordinate Maintenance Intervention and Continuing Operation](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt7---coordinate-maintenance-intervention-and-continuing-operation) | A qualified comparison of the complete outage with the supplied capacity and service conditions, including testing, restoration, hand-back and contingency. |
| What makes it possible to begin this protected intervention? | [MNT.8 - Isolate, Make Safe, and Authorize the Maintenance Intervention](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt8---isolate-make-safe-and-authorize-the-maintenance-intervention) | The actual isolation, protection and bounded permission for the selected act, or its unmet condition. A work order alone establishes none of them. |
| What intervention actually took place, and what state did it leave? | [MNT.9 - Perform and Record the Maintenance Intervention](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt9---perform-and-record-the-maintenance-intervention) | Performed-work and actual-configuration evidence, including consequential deviations and interruptions; a plan is not that evidence. |
| Has the required functioning been restored? | [MNT.10 - Verify Restored Functioning after Maintenance](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt10---verify-restored-functioning-after-maintenance) | A functioning result for the actual configuration, representative use and qualified acceptance basis; broader duty and resumed-use permission remain separate. |
| Who can resume which use of the returned equipment? | [MNT.11 - Hand Back and Authorize Resumed Use after Maintenance, with Certification Where Required](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt11---hand-back-and-authorize-resumed-use-after-maintenance-with-certification-where-required) | A reconciled returned state, control transfer and applicable resumed-use decision. A successful test does not automatically supply the authority. |
| Which history applies to this installed component and configuration? | [MNT.12 - Maintain Maintenance Information and Configuration Continuity](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt12---maintain-maintenance-information-and-configuration-continuity) | Maintenance-event and configuration continuity for the receiving question, including contradictions that change what can be inferred. |
| Do fleet results justify changing or retaining the programme? | [MNT.13 - Coordinate the Maintenance Programme and Fleet Learning](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt13---coordinate-the-maintenance-programme-and-fleet-learning) | An exposure- and event-qualified comparison and supported programme decision. Raw counts alone establish neither a fair rate comparison nor a causal policy advantage. |
| Should we retain, revise or replace this maintenance Method or tool? | [MNT.14 - Compare Maintenance Methods for Retention or Change](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt14---compare-maintenance-methods-for-retention-or-change) | A same-result comparison and supported retain, revise, replace, branch or stop decision. A new trial is conditional on an attainable, decision-changing answer worth its whole burden. |
| Why can two individually feasible jobs not be carried out together? | [MNT.15 - Reconcile Simultaneous Maintenance, Operation, and Support Work](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt15---reconcile-simultaneous-maintenance-operation-and-support-work) | A whole-combination account of shared specialists, capacity, fallback and protection, with a feasible allocation or timing change, or the exact unmet commitment. |
| Is the revised maintenance practice actually being continued or changed? | [MNT.16 - Deliberately Continue and Change Maintenance Culture](MAINTENANCE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#mnt16---deliberately-continue-and-change-maintenance-culture) | An account distinguishing access, transmission, actual enactment and effects, with a supported continuation or change decision; a new manual is not proof of changed practice. |

A maintenance question can concern one pump or a fleet: it seeks a maintenance policy, intervention or programme result that preserves or restores required functioning. Choosing continued use, renewal, replacement, repurposing or withdrawal by value, costs, risks and service effects is a distinct asset-management question even for one pump. For that comparison, open [Engineering Asset Management](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam-asset---compare-continued-use-and-change-for-one-asset), starting with EAM.8 and the applicable asset and service basis. A verb such as “replace”, a long horizon or a large asset count does not settle which result is needed.

Stop when the requested result is adequate. Selected equipment work still needs its applicable procedures, competent means, protection and authority. The MNT cases are constructed teaching examples, not field validation, equipment instructions or permission.


### Engineering.Reference:1.26 - Choose how to use and change engineered assets

The [Engineering Asset Management DPF](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) helps compare value, service, costs and risks over the lives of engineered assets. The question can concern one pump, an interacting asset system or a portfolio. Its sixteen patterns support the questions below; enter with the result you need and the inputs already available.

Four practical entries show connected use:

- [Compare continued use and change for one asset](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam-asset---compare-continued-use-and-change-for-one-asset): use EAM.8 for the alternatives and EAM.1 when the question or boundary needs clarification. A supported recommendation can complete an advice request; EAM.12 supplies the separate asset-decision work.
- [Choose asset work under shared constraints](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam-combination---choose-asset-work-under-shared-constraints): use EAM.10 with EAM.9 for conflicts and EAM.11 for timing. Obtain a feasible programme recommendation or identify the condition requiring another option or decision.
- [Reconsider a decision after a changed condition](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam-change---reconsider-a-decision-after-a-changed-condition): use EAM.13 and return to the affected information, demand, condition or capability assessment. Retain an adequate plan; investigate further when the attainable answer can usefully change it.
- [Improve how asset decisions are made](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam-practice---improve-how-asset-decisions-are-made): use EAM.14 for organizational provision, EAM.15 for reusable methods and EAM.16 for the practice people continue or change. Identify which contribution explains the recurring difficulty before selecting a change.

In the CityWater worked case, replacing pump D is preferable in the single-asset comparison, while the programme under a shared capital limit continues D and modifies C. The two recommendations answer different questions with different constraints. For a condition or maintained-functioning result used in such a comparison, return to the [maintenance methods](#engineeringreference125---maintain-equipment-and-manage-maintenance).

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which options should we compare for this asset or portfolio, for what service and period? | [EAM.1 - Frame the Engineered Assets and Required Outcomes](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam1---frame-the-engineered-assets-and-required-outcomes) | Agree the asset options, required service, comparison period and decision maker. |
| What required contribution must the assets support? | [EAM.2 - Relate Assets to Strategy, Services, and Required Capability](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam2---relate-assets-to-strategy-services-and-required-capability) | Relate proposed asset work to an actual service outcome and its authority. |
| Which information applies to this asset and comparison? | [EAM.3 - Establish the Asset Information and Configuration Basis](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam3---establish-the-asset-information-and-configuration-basis) | Resolve the answer-changing mismatch with a sufficient information basis. |
| What service will be needed under the conditions that matter? | [EAM.4 - Assess Demand and Service Need for Asset Decisions](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam4---assess-demand-and-service-need-for-asset-decisions) | Separate demand evidence and forecasts from the mandated service. |
| What do observed condition and delivered performance support? | [EAM.5 - Assess Asset Condition and Performance](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam5---assess-asset-condition-and-performance) | Return a qualified account for the asset decision. |
| Can the assets support service during normal use and disturbance? | [EAM.6 - Assess Asset Capacity, Resilience, and Interdependence](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam6---assess-asset-capacity-resilience-and-interdependence) | Compare required service with qualified available capability and fallback. |
| Which acquisition or change can provide the needed contribution? | [EAM.7 - Generate Ways to Supply an Asset-Dependent Service](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam7---generate-ways-to-supply-an-asset-dependent-service) | Generate comparable qualified alternatives with their whole burden. |
| Which continued-use or change option is worth considering? | [EAM.8 - Generate Maintenance, Renewal, and Retirement Alternatives](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam8---generate-maintenance-renewal-and-retirement-alternatives) | Compare supported policies at a common service, horizon and cost basis. |
| Which asset alternative is supported, and what unresolved conflict remains? | [EAM.9 - Compare Asset Alternatives and Reconcile Decisions When They Conflict](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam9---compare-asset-alternatives-and-reconcile-decisions-when-they-conflict) | Compare eligible asset alternatives and identify any conflicting service, funding or work condition and the decision needed to resolve it. |
| Which eligible asset combination should receive the allocation? | [EAM.10 - Compare Engineered-Asset Portfolio Combinations](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam10---compare-engineered-asset-portfolio-combinations) | Compare complete programmes under the actual binding conditions. |
| Can the selected programme be completed while preserving service? | [EAM.11 - Time Asset Interventions and Manage Dependencies](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam11---time-asset-interventions-and-manage-dependencies) | Construct a supported calendar or expose the limiting prerequisite. |
| What supported answer is requested and who makes the asset decision? | [EAM.12 - Integrate Specialist Results for an Asset Recommendation or Decision](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam12---integrate-specialist-results-for-an-asset-recommendation-or-decision) | Integrate applicable results and distinguish advice from actual authorization. |
| What has actually changed, and should the asset plan be retained or revised? | [EAM.13 - Track Realized Outcomes and Reconsider Asset Plans](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam13---track-realized-outcomes-and-reconsider-asset-plans) | Compare obtained outcomes with the decision premises at the same scope. |
| What in the organization of asset work prevents timely, supported decisions? | [EAM.14 - Decide Whether and How to Change the Asset-Management System](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam14---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-the-asset-management-system) | Compare feasible changes to responsibilities, information flow or support with keeping the current arrangement. |
| Should this way of making asset decisions be retained or changed? | [EAM.15 - Decide Whether and How to Change Engineering Asset-Management Methods](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam15---decide-whether-and-how-to-change-engineering-asset-management-methods) | Compare ways of answering the same asset question, including the effort of applying and maintaining them. |
| Which asset-management practices do people use, and should they continue or change? | [EAM.16 - Deliberately Continue and Change Engineering Asset-Management Culture](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eam16---deliberately-continue-and-change-engineering-asset-management-culture) | Establish what the evidence supports and compare continuation, change, a qualified branch or stopping. |

Use the [qualified returns from related practice](ENGINEERING-ASSET-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#eamreference2---qualified-returns-from-related-practice) to connect maintenance condition and intervention results, operating service and capacity, engineering alternatives and configuration, organizational ability, and method or cultural development. Preserve the asset and configuration, receiving use, period, assumptions and limits that make each result applicable. The source table gives the exact supplying and receiving patterns.

The worked cases state their supplied service requirements, engineering possibilities, finance assumptions and decision authority. In an actual project, obtain those inputs from the responsible practice and decision makers. A pattern's method helps produce or examine a result; the case's inputs remain assumptions of that case.


### Engineering.Reference:1.27 - Qualify a research question or choose a design

The [Research Method Practice DPF](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) supplies `RMP.1`–`RMP.9`. Start here to decide whether a request needs research and to choose a criticism-bearing design or an honest stop. The following sections cover [operationalization and the actual trace](#engineeringreference128---make-research-executable-and-inspect-its-course), [claim analysis and relevant credibility work](#engineeringreference129---analyze-a-claim-or-examine-its-credibility), and [retaining or improving a research Method](#engineeringreference130---retain-or-improve-a-research-method). Supplied inputs allow direct entry at the question you need to answer.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does the request need new research, already have a sufficient answer, or require a different kind of work? | [RMP.1 - Decide Whether a Question Needs Research and When to Stop](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp1--decide-whether-a-question-needs-research-and-when-to-stop) | A scoped research question; a sufficient answer from available sources; a request to the practice able to answer; or a statement of the missing input that prevents a decision. |
| Is the existing evidence sufficient, is a new study worth doing, or does a missing result prevent choosing? | [RMP.2 - Choose a Criticism-Bearing Research Design or Stop](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp2--choose-a-criticism-bearing-research-design-or-stop) | An adequate answer from existing evidence; a justified research design; a hold identifying the input that prevents selection; or a justified choice of no new study, with the unresolved claim, limits and conditions for reconsideration explicit. |
| How can a manager obtain and use a defensible test of a workplace change? | [Workplace experiment: an additional approver](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmpapplication5---app-rmp-05--should-a-second-approver-reduce-customer-waiting) | A worked application from suitable event records through a qualified comparison and its result to a staffing decision, including when a shared queue requires a different comparison and when to stop without a new study. |

The complete repertoire supplies guidance for obtaining research results, not already obtained results. If a needed field-specific result, permission or evidence is missing, name that gap and return it to its owner. A protocol or collected information alone does not establish the research result.


### Engineering.Reference:1.28 - Make research executable and inspect its course

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How will the selected design become particular observations, source work or computations? | [RMP.3 - Operationalize the Research Design without Replacing the Question](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp3---operationalize-the-research-design-without-replacing-the-question) | A usable protocol with the research reasons for its consequential choices, or the exact unsupported operation and its missing input. Reuse a qualified protocol when it fits. Return a defeated design premise to RMP.2 and a changed question to RMP.1; retain the supported part. |
| How do we preserve or recover the records needed to examine this inquiry? | [RMP.4 - Preserve a Criticism-Ready Research Trace](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp4---preserve-a-criticism-ready-research-trace) | An inspectable account connecting actual conduct to its material, or an exact limitation caused by loss, reconstruction or restricted access. Enter during ongoing work or directly with inherited records. Use adequate existing records without creating another protocol. Stop with the supported examination or its precise limitation. |

Operationalization specifies intended work; the trace accounts for actual work and retained material. They can develop together. A trace can identify a lost comparison without making that comparison available.


### Engineering.Reference:1.29 - Analyze a claim or examine its credibility

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How should I interpret a source, and which earlier conclusions or actions change with the reading? | [Interpret a source and revise what follows](#engineeringreference23---interpret-a-source-and-revise-what-follows) | A source reading carried into the receiving decision, with affected earlier conclusions revised and unresolved questions kept explicit. |
| What claim does this material support, and which criticism changes the answer? | [RMP.5 - Analyze and Criticize the Research Claim under Its Method](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp5---analyze-and-criticize-the-research-claim-under-its-method) | A bounded claim with the criticism actually performed and its remaining limits. Reuse adequate analysis; retain a supported result when its stronger interpretation fails. Stop with a sufficient qualified answer. |
| Which credibility examination could change this claim's use, and is it worth obtaining? | [RMP.6 - Choose a Credibility Test That Bears on the Research Claim, or Answer without New Testing](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp6---choose-a-credibility-test-that-bears-on-the-research-claim-or-answer-without-new-testing) | An adequate existing result, a selected relevant examination, a qualified answer without new testing, or the exact missing input that prevents this selection. Select new work only for its worthwhile obtainable contribution; selection is not an observed result. |

Enter RMP.5 with an adequate supplied analysis or with inherited material whose origin, Method and limits can be recovered for the present question. Return to RMP.1–RMP.4 only for the particular question, design premise, operational choice or trace that the examination lacks.

For RMP.6, bring the bounded claim, its basis, proposed use and a live threat. Compatible direct inputs need no new RMP.5 run. Match the examination to that threat and compare its attainable contribution with the whole burden of obtaining and interpreting it. Use the relevant domain criteria and obtain any required permission from its responsible authority.

For example, a model reproduces its reported output, but the available comparison does not justify a field maintenance interval. RMP.5 can return the supported computation with the field claim unresolved. In RMP.6, another identical rerun cannot answer that field-use question. An obtainable, worthwhile comparison with suitable field data can justify selecting validation under domain criteria. Otherwise, end the appraisal with the supported computation and the unresolved field-use claim. Test selection supplies no observed result, and the maintenance authority retains the interval decision.

When the needed result is what an evidence corpus jointly warrants, open [RMP.7 - Synthesize a Research Evidence Corpus](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp7---synthesize-a-research-evidence-corpus). For deciding whether to retain or revise an identified claim or model contribution and returning the evidence its recipient needs, open [RMP.8 - Use Research Results to Retain or Revise an Episteme's Claims and Return Bounded Evidence](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp8---use-research-results-to-retain-or-revise-an-epistemes-claims-and-return-bounded-evidence). They can use compatible supplied results. Stop after RMP.5 or RMP.6 when its answer already resolves the current question.


### Engineering.Reference:1.30 - Retain or improve a research Method

Actual research work, criticism, a changed tool or new receiving conditions can raise a Method question. First distinguish the reusable Method from its description, implementation, available capability and the particular analysis or claim. A disappointing finding or software release alone does not establish that the Method failed.

| Your question | Open | What you can obtain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Should we retain, correct or change this research Method, and what follows for existing results? | [RMP.9 - Decide Whether and How to Improve Research Methods and Practice](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp9--decide-whether-and-how-to-improve-research-methods-and-practice) | Supported retention, a verified bounded correction, a justified Method change, or a restriction on unsupported use. When qualification remains unresolved, the result may instead select worthwhile obtainable evidence while preserving that unresolved question. |

Bring the research use, difficulty, current Method and available basis. Finish with an adequate existing answer or determinate correction. Select a further comparison only when different results could change the decision, the comparison is attainable and its whole burden is warranted. Declining that work does not establish Method adequacy; keep unsupported use restricted.

For example, an accepted sample-variance Method for n independent observations divides the squared-deviation sum by n−1. If software uses n instead, correct and check the implementation and its dependent analysis. Under those premises, the Method can stay unchanged without another efficacy study. If the receiving situation instead violates the Method's assumptions, that correction cannot qualify the new use. A warranted comparison can be selected, but its planned result is not evidence already obtained.

Use [Method Engineering](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) only for the identity, trial, fit, worth, variant or introduction contribution this question needs. Preserve the research purpose and its appropriate criticism; a common score need not fit statistical, interpretive and historical inquiry.

Return changed operations to RMP.3, affected records to RMP.4, a changed analysis or open credibility choice to RMP.5 or RMP.6, and changed synthesis to RMP.7. Reopen only the contribution actually affected; return an affected claim or model to [RMP.8](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/RESEARCH-METHOD-PRACTICE-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#rmp8---use-research-results-to-retain-or-revise-an-epistemes-claims-and-return-bounded-evidence). A correction confined to an analysis or claim stays with RMP.5 or RMP.8. Reopen RMP.1 only when the Method difficulty meets its research-membership conditions. The decision to change a Method, its actual introduction and evidence of its effects remain different results.


## Engineering.Reference:2 - Why examine a handover that arrives on time?

In this constructed case, the maintenance team delivers its schedule on time. During an ordinary handover, the preparer follows one equipment entry into the receiver's use. Twelve names have been manually translated because the incoming abbreviations differ from those used at the site. Nobody had regarded this successful compensation as a problem.

The receiving question is whether the schedule identifies the intended equipment without depending on one person's memory. A suggestion to improve deadline reminders leaves that question untouched. [B.5.PI](../FPF-Spec.md#b5pi---initiate-inquiry-from-ongoing-work) retains the discrepancy between the proposed advice and the work; [B.5.EA](../FPF-Spec.md#b5ea---articulate-a-working-distinction-from-experience) helps if the preparer can point to the retyping but cannot yet name the missing relation. The team need not request a full audit or search for the name of a semantic-integration method.

An authoritative equipment list is available in this case. Comparison resolves ten entries. Two abbreviations name different equipment in different buildings, so a context-free replacement would remove a distinction the schedule needs. The [semantic-integration methods](#engineeringreference16---connect-separately-governed-meanings-and-representations) can develop the correspondence if the available list and ordinary comparison are insufficient. For this handover, obtain the missing building context and give the receiver usable identities; do not defer the schedule until a complete terminology project is finished.

For repeated work, [ME.1 and ME.3](#engineeringreference17---improve-a-method-or-an-organization) can frame what a revised preparation method must preserve. [ME.8–ME.10](#engineeringreference17---improve-a-method-or-an-organization) can make the correspondence and its use accessible; [ME.14](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#me14---evaluate-a-methods-practical-worth-against-current-alternatives) compares that change with continuing the successful manual method. These are conditional contributions, not compulsory next stages. Preparing and maintaining a shared mapping may be unjustified for one remaining handover.

If the receiver needs an explanation of the building distinction, obtain an explanation for that question. If staff understand it but cannot apply it to unfamiliar entries, [HCD](#engineeringreference112---develop-a-practice-or-a-persons-capability) can develop that human capability. Supplying an AI assistant with the equipment list instead changes its available information; it does not establish either human learning or parameter learning. The schedule preparation, interpretation and coordination must work together while the handover is performed, as the method vertical in [B.1.5.EW](../FPF-Spec.md#b15ew---recover-how-constituent-actions-enact-encompassing-work) makes explicit.

Return to the receiving work: can the receiver identify the equipment, and which entries still depend on unavailable context? If the receiver instead demonstrates that both conventions were already understood and retyping changed only typography, withdraw the identity diagnosis. The remaining question is whether removing that effort is worthwhile. If the relevant records cannot be inspected now, retain the dependency as an early cue and name the missing access; do not claim a validated replacement. A justified continuation without change is an acceptable result.


## Engineering.Reference:3 - Should SensorCo prepare a service trial or continue with devices?

SensorCo's device and service contracts remain viable for the next twelve months. Its strategy team is comparing device-only continuation with a new integrated service. Six interested customers and two trial discussions are not paid demand. [The complete constructed Strategy case](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#strapplication1---app-str-01---choose-sensorcos-response-to-commoditized-ai-inspection) supplies the assumptions and alternatives.

[PSD.10](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/PROBLEM-STRUCTURING-AND-DECISION-SUPPORT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#psd10---represent-decision-relevant-uncertainty-and-evidence-limits) helps state the decision-relevant uncertainty. [STR.7](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str7---decide-whether-and-how-to-experiment-while-preserving-strategic-options) asks whether more evidence can change the choice enough to justify obtaining it. If full costing makes every feasible service alternative inferior to device-only continuation under the stated criterion, the comparison can finish without a trial. Incomplete costing leaves that comparison open. A customer-data experiment cannot supply permission to use those data.

The team recommends four internal preparation days, displacing a four-day device-diagnostic improvement. The Board authorizes those four days from an eight-day preparation/use envelope. [STR.11](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str11---select-strategy-portfolio-commitments-and-assumptions) keeps that authorization distinct from trial execution, all eighteen proposed development days and the still-open twelve-month direction.

A later shared-work comparison has eighty internal person-days. Service, reserve, trial work, platform work and learning would demand ninety. A reduced proposal totals seventy-eight, retaining the eight-day reserve. Two of its six platform days preserve a device-compatible fallback; they are already counted, not the two unallocated days. [STR.14](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str14---reconcile-simultaneous-strategic-work-across-horizons-and-scales) also checks when qualified people are needed: a monthly total can fit while Tuesday needs ten qualified analyst-hours and only eight are available.

[STR.8](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str8---relate-capabilities-dependencies-business-models-and-initiatives) identifies the contributions needed for the selected option. [OCE.9](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce9---realize-a-bounded-organization-capability-increment) guides an organization-capability increment; [HCD](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#table-of-contents) guides the needed human-capability development; the platform provider must supply tools and access. Each contribution has its own conditions and evidence. The seventy-eight-day arithmetic neither demonstrates those capabilities nor authorizes the larger proposal.

The useful return now is the bounded preparation decision and its unresolved conditions. Independent preparation can proceed within its authority; missing data permission stops the dependent use. Use [STR.12](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/STRATEGY-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#str12---observe-signals-to-continue-or-reconsider-strategic-direction-and-commitments) when an observed change calls for reconsideration.


## Engineering.Reference:4 - How should we obtain climate control for a greenhouse?

An equipment company needs climate control for a new greenhouse. It could buy a ready controller, commission a custom controller, develop one internally with AI assistance, or combine a ready controller with its own supervisory layer.

**Start with [SYSE.24](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse24---choose-how-the-project-will-obtain-a-needed-engineering-result).** Compare ways to obtain the same accepted climate-control result. Include the integration and support work, required capability, access and eventual exit as well as the device price.

Identify the real greenhouse, crops, actuators, climate and operating conditions with [SYSE.1](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse1---choose-and-reopen-the-project-system-of-interest) and [SYSE.16](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse16---recover-the-systems-and-conditions-needed-for-a-use-decision) where needed. Obtain the actual performance and safety thresholds from the appropriate specialists.

| What could reverse the choice? | Evidence to obtain |
| --- | --- |
| Control performance or fallback fails in the intended configuration. | Configuration-specific control and electrical-safety thresholds, a permitted test, and evidence that the fallback works. |
| The attractive price hides a continuing access or support problem. | The actual offer, funding limit, access and update terms, data arrangements, support duties, remedies and exit costs over the intended period. |
| The receiving team cannot perform the work left to it. | A workable allocation among people, AI and providers, with assignments, authority and capability evidence. Identify any required human development. |
| The arrangement cannot be kept operating. | The maintenance, recovery, reliability and operating results required for the intended service, including capacity where it matters. |

The [GH-2 worked application](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syseapplication4---app-syse-04--worked-application-obtain-climate-control-for-a-new-greenhouse-configuration) follows this comparison. Two candidates remain; an interface-and-fallback test and the example's price-and-burden rule favour the ready controller with an internal supervisory layer. It leaves a further question: can the internal integration agent configure the layer and produce commissioning evidence before the need date?

Use the example to understand the comparison. For procurement, substitute your offers, configuration and evidence; have the responsible chooser record the resulting decision. [A.15.9](../FPF-Spec.md#a159---use-or-request-a-bounded-result-from-another-practice) helps request a missing specialist result when it could change the choice.

After selection, obtain the realization result through [SYSE.3](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse3---plan-the-next-system-realization-action-recursive-realization-network), configuration identity through [SYSE.13](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse13---establish-configuration-identity-variants-and-effectivity), and the required evidence and release decision through [SYSE.10](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse10---assess-research-model-and-trial-results-for-an-engineering-decision), [SYSE.4](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse4---decide-whether-and-how-to-challenge-an-engineering-claim) and [SYSE.14](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse14---make-a-release-decision-for-named-engineering-work-or-use) as those questions arise. If the integration or commissioning method is itself inadequate, use [ME.1](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#me1---choose-and-reopen-the-projects-method-engineering-focus) to investigate it. Once the arrangement and operating conditions are established, OPS.5-OPS.7 in the complete Operations Management DPF address admission, exceptional-case continuation and local priority or commitment revision.

Pause only the decision that depends on a missing input. Keep the conclusions whose grounds still hold.


## Engineering.Reference:5 - What should a small engineering team develop, obtain, or delegate?

A startup wants better engineering results and a stronger ability to compete. It is considering staff development, recruitment, providers, a method or platform change, and a different allocation of work among people, AI and robots.

**Name one needed result, then use [OCE.8](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce8---compare-human-ai-robotic-and-provider-arrangements-for-the-same-organizational-work-result).** “Use more AI” and “train the team” are still broad possibilities. Turn each useful possibility into a whole arrangement that could obtain the result. Keep the intended use, horizon, acceptance criteria and protected conditions the same across candidates.

Use representative work to recover how the team currently operates: who contributes, what they can do, what they are assigned and permitted to do, how contributions meet, and where failures or support burdens occur. [C.38](../FPF-Spec.md#c38---construct-comparable-ways-to-obtain-one-result) gives the general same-result comparison; OCE.8 supplies the organizational method.

| Possibility | What the comparison needs |
| --- | --- |
| Develop current members | The people and later work, current capability and transfer conditions, development time and opportunity cost. |
| Recruit or assign another performer | Demonstrated capability, eligibility, assignment, authority, resources and integration needs. |
| Obtain provider expertise | The provider's contribution and duties, acceptance evidence, data and knowledge custody, continued access, recovery and exit; the work left with the startup. |
| Change a method, interface or platform | Evidence of the limitation, a candidate change and a representative trial, including burdens shifted to others. |
| Combine human, AI and robotic contributions | Capability, assignments, permissions, interfaces, oversight, recovery, security and safety limits, and observations of the actual arrangement. |

Several domain questions may contribute. [ME.1](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#me1---choose-and-reopen-the-projects-method-engineering-focus) and [ME.3](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#me3---build-or-reconsider-situational-method-requirements-and-fit-criteria) clarify the method and required contribution; [ME.6](METHOD-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#me6---compare-method-architecture-alternatives-and-simultaneous-enactment-conflicts) compares method architectures. [SYSE.15](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse15---choose-and-refresh-the-engineering-methods-needed-by-a-project) and [SYSE.24](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse24---choose-how-the-project-will-obtain-a-needed-engineering-result) help with the engineering repertoire and ways to obtain the result. [SYSE.12](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse12---develop-or-retain-an-engineering-platform-for-practitioner-work) investigates a platform limitation, and [SYSE.20](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse20---reconcile-overlapping-engineering-work-and-required-order) helps reconcile overlapping work.

For capability claims, [A.2.2](../FPF-Spec.md#a22---system-capability-conditions-measures-and-fit) identifies whose capability is asserted and under what conditions. [E.23.CDI](../FPF-Spec.md#e23cdi---developing-capability-for-a-named-work-family) addresses development for a particular family of work. [A.15.8](../FPF-Spec.md#a158---work-performance-configuration-and-recovery-testing) helps when the performing configuration or recovery changes the answer; [A.13](../FPF-Spec.md#a13---the-agential-role--agency-spectrum) and [A.15.1](../FPF-Spec.md#a151---uwork-dated-performed-work-occurrence) distinguish the performer and actual work. Human demand, diagnosis and profile questions in this Reference can use the separate complete HCD publication.

Obtain a strategy, finance, legal, safety, maintenance or other specialist answer when it can change this comparison. State the particular question in the request. The organization makes its choice from the resulting comparison: select an arrangement, conduct a useful authorized probe, reject the candidates, or identify the evidence still needed.

Before dependent work begins, establish its required capability, assignment, permission and authority, and the evidence for protected conditions. Once the operating arrangement exists, OPS.5–OPS.7 can address its narrower admission, case-continuation and priority questions.


## Engineering.Reference:6 - Connect contributions, concerns and consequences across a whole project

Use this answer when capable specialists produce locally satisfactory results, yet the project cannot obtain a usable whole, or when the organization must change how it obtains those contributions. **Start with the result someone needs to use; recover the work and relations that make it obtainable; then compare the arrangements and their consequences.** A useful first return can be the exact missing contribution and who can supply it. A sufficient specialist answer can already settle the question.


### Engineering.Reference:6.1 - Recover the needed contribution from the whole result

In this constructed case, an instrument maker must demonstrate that two modules work together under an agreed acceptance condition. Two teams design the modules. A shared laboratory provides a rig and specialist, and the stipulated acceptance rule requires judgement independent of the design work. Both modules pass their local tests, but their fastening interfaces have incompatible dimensions. The local results therefore leave the intended integrated use unsupported.

For this offering project, the system to be brought about is the integrated instrument. Its intended use, configuration and acceptance question determine what each contribution must establish. [SYSE.1](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse1---choose-and-reopen-the-project-system-of-interest) helps recover that project-relative subject when it is unclear. The laboratory is a provider to this project; its continuing service has its own recipients and commitments.

Ask the engineers to recover the common interface conditions and which design choices were fixed or left open. Obtain the missing mechanical judgement about a compatible fastening arrangement. [SYSE.9](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse9---use-or-request-specialist-engineering-results) makes the request precise: which configuration and use it concerns, what result is needed, and what the engineering decision will do with it. Qualified mechanical practice supplies the fastening and test Methods. [SYSE.6](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse6---decide-and-reopen-the-engineering-architecture) connects the choice to the whole instrument: compare the consequences, decide the shared constraint under the relevant authority, and leave unaffected module details with their contributors. Suppose the qualified engineering comparison supports a common mounting pattern. The decision selects that interface and the integrated test needed to judge it; both teams update to the identified configuration C7.

General engineering reasoning makes the whole, its use, interfaces and evidence dependencies explicit. It helps find the professional work still needed. The particular calculation, physical test and interpretation need their own Methods and capable performers. “Mechanical engineer” is useful for finding professional knowledge and possible contributors; the present contribution is the justified interface answer for this configuration. A role name alone establishes neither that answer nor the person's capability to produce it.

Follow the result through its receiving use:

| Contribution in this case | What another participant needs from it |
| --- | --- |
| Module design and integration | A compatible configuration and the identified conditions under which the modules must work together. |
| Laboratory service | A feasible test arrangement with the required rig, specialist, inputs and usable interval; subsequently, the performed test and its returned evidence. |
| Evidence integration | An accessible package identifying the tested configuration, relevant results, limits and unresolved claims. |
| Independent acceptance judgement | A supported acceptance or reasoned return under the stipulated criteria and authority. A return identifies the claim or condition that prevents acceptance. |

Follow the relations within the work as well as its timing. While a specialist interprets a trace, that interpretation can contribute to judging an interface claim within preparation of the whole acceptance package. The integrated-use question determines what the trace must establish. Meanwhile, booking the laboratory enables the test without itself performing the test or the acceptance judgement. A test description, the ability to use it, actual test Work and the resulting report supply different parts of this account.


### Engineering.Reference:6.2 - Resolve the conflict at the relation that failed

One person may design and integrate if the combined work fits their capability, assignment and available time. Under this case's independent-acceptance rule, that designer cannot also supply the required independent judgement. A senior technician proposed as a replacement test performer must fit the actual test and its admission conditions; seniority alone supplies no substitution basis. FPF [E.10.ROLE](../FPF-Spec.md#e10role---recovering-what-role-means-in-the-current-claim) and [A.2.7](../FPF-Spec.md#a27---systemrolekindrelationstructure---relations-among-system-role-kinds) help unpack “combined role”: which assignments may share a holder, which require different holders, and how the Methods or work combine. Use these relations instead of treating role labels as parts of the person or project.

Now suppose the returned report concerns configuration C6, preceding the interface repair. The receiver needs applicable evidence for the C7 claim. Another reviewer appointment cannot make that report applicable. Preserve any results whose conditions still fit, and obtain only the missing evidence or justified applicability account.

Participants can also disagree for different reasons. The department head wants an earlier date, a designer objects that the proposed interface violates a required tolerance, and the laboratory manager reports that the needed interval is already committed. Recover the grounds of each statement. The tolerance needs an engineering answer; allocation of laboratory time needs the provider's decision and a feasible service plan; a proposed change of date needs agreement by the parties whose commitment changes. Ask each receiver what the proposed repair lets them do and what it leaves impossible.

Professional concerns help discover relevant characteristics, but inspect the actual concern. A low quoted test price can coexist with higher total cost after preparation, transport, support and displaced work. Specify which cost and period the comparison uses. Keep a protected technical condition distinct from a preference that the authorized parties can trade. The [Leadership DPF](https://github.com/ailev/FPF/blob/main/Development%20DPF%20Suite/LEADERSHIP-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md) develops the needed explanation, challenge and negotiation through LDR.1–LDR.3. Its results identify changed contributions; actual assignments and support still have to be obtained through their owners.


### Engineering.Reference:6.3 - Carry the reasoning into a project that changes the organization

Suppose the instrument maker repeatedly relies on the same manager to reconstruct missing inputs, find a laboratory interval and obtain an acceptance return. Management now wants the engineering organization to obtain that complete contribution with less exceptional intervention. This is a second project. Its changed system is the engineering organization; its result is a workable arrangement for obtaining contributions across the module teams, laboratory and acceptance work. The instrument remains the subject of the offering project. The integrator's ability to interpret a trace is a further question for human capability development.

Recover the organization's intended contribution through [OCE.1](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce1---identify-the-changed-organization-and-intended-contribution), then use [OCE.2](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce2---recover-current-organization-work-and-arrangement) to examine how representative work actually reaches its receiver, including informal help. A report may be complete while the next participant is still waiting: they may lack its location, version identity or notice that it is ready. Faster testing would leave that delivery difficulty unresolved. Recover the request, promise, production, recognizable return, acceptance and correction path together.

The general questions transfer: what whole must work, what result is needed, which relations make it obtainable, and which consequence would defeat the arrangement? Their domain answers change. A fastening calculation addresses the instrument. Contribution design, position establishment and effective appointments address the organization. Similar titles such as “architect” in the two projects do not establish corresponding Methods. [C.32.MWA](../FPF-Spec.md#c32mwa---synthesize-an-architecture-account-of-methods-and-their-use) helps compare ways to organize Method, Work, capability and provider relations, including the burden an arrangement moves to other work. Use the OCE Methods for the organization decisions.

Apply [OCE.7](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce7---coordinate-product-or-service-and-organization-architecture-decisions) when the instrument and organization choices constrain each other. Compare changing the organization, changing the product, changing both, and retaining their different boundaries with explicit coordination. In this case, suppose merging the groups would disrupt a specialist-service commitment, while separating the shared test requires a redesign that cannot fit the next two releases. Retaining the module teams with one integration contribution and an agreed laboratory service is then a serious candidate. Its cost is shared-test coordination, and each group's release depends on the joint result.

The engineering and organization decision-makers each decide within their authority. The product decision retains the module and test boundaries; the organization decision selects how the integration contribution and exception return will work. Reopen the pair if the shared test burden defeats the protected service commitment, or when the two-release horizon ends. The laboratory provider still has to make the resource decision on which this choice depends. If it cannot, the preferred arrangement remains unsupported.


### Engineering.Reference:6.4 - Establish and exercise the arrangement

Use [OCE.4](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce4---design-an-organizations-contribution-architecture) to design the contribution path for the selected arrangement. Specify who supplies the identified package, who uses it, what makes it usable, how an unsupported claim returns for correction, and which timing and support conditions must hold. Keep separate specialist, evidence and acceptance decisions where the work requires them. If a continuing position must remain identifiable through vacancy or holder replacement, [OCE.5](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce5---define-organization-positions) supplies its institutional basis and expected contribution. A direct assignment can suffice when no such position identity matters.

Then use [OCE.6](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce6---establish-holder-assignments-and-enabling-relations-for-organization-change) to establish the actual appointment and the separately needed authority, access and provision. In the case, the evidence integrator's appointment can be effective while repository access is still pending. The appointment remains effective, but package preparation cannot rely on unavailable access. Naming someone responsible does not allocate the laboratory, supply specialist capability or change the acceptance rule.

Suppose the integrator can assemble the package but cannot interpret a newly required trace. Compare a missing skill with a misleading description, unsuitable test, missing access or incompatible workload through [HCD.3](../Development%20DPF%20Suite/HUMAN-CAPABILITY-DEVELOPMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#hcd3--diagnose-whether-a-capability-misconception-or-behaviour-limits-work). Use compatible existing observations; obtain a distinguishing observation only when needed. For a supported learning need, give a qualified learning provider the trace-interpretation task, required grounds and later conditions of use. Obtain practice and feedback against those criteria, with the time, tools and later opportunity required. A capable specialist can instead supply the interpretation when that arrangement meets the receiving conditions. A checklist or reminder permitted in the work can remain part of supported performance. The change organizer also needs the expertise to distinguish these causes; obtain qualified engineering or learning help when that judgement is beyond their capability.

Use [OCE.11](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce11---coordinate-organization-change-work-with-continuing-service) to fit the complete change into continuing work. Package preparation, practice, specialist feedback, test setup, ordinary service and recovery can compete for the same people and interval. A learning proposal without released time leaves the contribution unavailable. [OPS.13](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops13---align-commitments-resources-and-service-outcomes) connects the service promise to that complete work and resource basis, including acceptance. Keep any old obligation visible until the authorized parties accept a revision.

Use [OCE.9](ORGANIZATION-CHANGE-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#oce9---realize-a-bounded-organization-capability-increment) to exercise a small complete use under the selected design and trial conditions. A team requests the test; the provider confirms feasible conditions; the test produces evidence; the integrator returns the identified package; the independent contributor accepts it or gives a reasoned correction. Exercise an unusable return as well as an ordinary success. If the report exists but its receiver cannot find the current version, repair that crossing and repeat it within the whole contribution.

Observe later work under the conditions the organization needs to rely on. If reduced dependence on the initiating manager matters, include an episode without that manager reconstructing the path. Retain any allowed specialist help. A successful facilitated attempt supports what happened with that help; it does not establish the less dependent capability. The operating owner accepts the continuing service and support consequences. Completing the organization project does not discharge outstanding instrument or laboratory commitments.


### Engineering.Reference:6.5 - Reconsider the affected choice when conditions change

Withdraw the laboratory interval. The prior service plan no longer supplies the intended test in that period. Return the consequence to the provider and service owner while an alternative interval, provider, test arrangement or agreed date remains possible. Carry any changed engineering conditions back to the engineer: a different test can change what its evidence supports. Preserve unaffected module work and compatible evidence.

Withdraw acceptance authority instead. Obtain the required authority decision or another eligible, capable and authorized contributor under the independence rule. Extra laboratory hours leave that gap open. If authority remains but later work requires recognizing an unfamiliar trace problem without a prompt, return the changed demand and observations to HCD.3. Where an ordinary reminder is allowed and sufficient, preserve that supported arrangement; require self-initiated recognition only when the work needs it.

A repair can expose another conflict. Return to the lost-interval case, with the other required contributions still available. Suppose an alternative provider offers a night test with the required rig and specialist. The proposed interval fits the test work, while a preliminary site account indicates possible disturbance to a nearby resident. That person performs no project work and cannot attend the meeting. Their possible loss still belongs in the choice. [SYSE.17](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse17---find-systems-that-may-bear-engineering-consequences) helps trace the exposure, state what is known and uncertain, and return the consequence to the decision that can alter it. The preliminary account is no measurement of the proposed test.

Compare an available daytime interval or quieter arrangement, using [SYSE.2](SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#syse2---develop-linked-use-and-system-concepts) if the new consequence changes the linked use or system concept. Obtain a bounded acoustic or other specialist result when it can change the decision and warrants its full burden. Permission and any needed representation of the resident require their own basis. A technically successful test would settle neither the disturbance question nor the relevant permission. Feed the resulting constraint or uncertainty into the laboratory and organization choice, retaining the valid engineering work.

Finish this inquiry when the next useful result, its receiving use and obtainable contribution are clear enough to act, or when the exact missing condition and return are known. Ordinary coordination can suffice without an organization-change project.


## Engineering.Reference:7 - How should we set a target and judge a miss after conditions change?

A repair cooperative wants customers' equipment back in useful service, with accepted quality, agreed dates and enough means to keep operating. A manager proposes a completion target; Finance needs an honest forecast; the person allocating technicians needs a resource decision. Later, a missed target must inform an assessment. Treating one number as all four answers can make the work look coherent while its participants cannot act on it.

Use [OPS.21](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops21---choose-operating-aims-targets-and-comparisons) to construct the aim and comparison when they are missing, [MA.5–6](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma5---construct-and-update-an-operating-forecast) to obtain and preserve the conditional outlook, [OPS.13](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops13---align-commitments-resources-and-service-outcomes) to establish actual service commitments, and [OPS.22](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops22---interpret-operating-performance-and-decide-the-response) to interpret the later result. Start with an adequate supplied contribution wherever one exists. The connection is: **choose the useful change and its comparison; keep the outlook honest; make the response jointly possible; examine the actual result and response; revise the affected aim or arrangement.**


### Engineering.Reference:7.1 - Construct the ambition from the receiving work

All quantities, evidence and authorities in this example are stipulated. Twelve identified customers have equipment that could usefully return to service this month through the cooperative's standard repair. Five have booked. Seven have qualified offers; an adequate nonoverlapping demand account supports three further acceptances under current conditions. The forecast is therefore eight, with the remaining acceptances uncertain. The twelve opportunities include those eight; they are not additional demand.

OPS.21 begins before choosing an indicator. Useful restored equipment is the result. Counting closed tickets alone could reward incomplete repairs or avoiding difficult cases. The team therefore compares accepted repairs in this named customer population by month end, retaining quality evidence, unfinished cases and any later returns that could defeat the claim. Continuing service for existing recipients remains protected.

Eight, ten, twelve and fourteen now have different grounds. Eight describes the expected result and leaves four known needs beyond it. Ten would serve two further needs within the base provision calculated below. Twelve would address every identified suitable need if the customers choose repair and the cooperative obtains the means. Fourteen has no additional identified useful demand or way to serve it in this case. The team provisionally chooses twelve as an ambition, conditional on those needs remaining useful, customer choice and a worthwhile resource arrangement; its first action is to clarify the seven offers. This is a reasoned choice of ambition, not a claim that twelve is already likely or promised. A customer whose need disappears should not be sold an unwanted repair to protect the count.

The cooperative does not use a peer league table here: another team's mix, starting position and shared support have not been shown comparable. It can retain other observations without making each a new improvement target. A different operation could reasonably choose a range, a qualified milestone or observation without a numerical quota; OPS.21 explains those alternatives.


### Engineering.Reference:7.2 - Join the ambition to provision and dated money

The base team has 36 usable hours after separately protected continuing service. The stated work includes six setup hours plus three hours per standard repair, including completion and acceptance work. One obtainable staffed block adds eight usable hours for 180 monetary units. Using the operating capacity account, [MA.1](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma1---build-the-resource-consumption-and-cost-model) and [MA.2](MANAGEMENT-ACCOUNTING-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ma2---explain-the-cost-and-use-of-capacity) give:

| Work under the initial standard-repair assumptions | Hours needed | Provision that could support it |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Eight repairs | 6 + 8 × 3 = 30 | The base 36 hours |
| Ten repairs | 6 + 10 × 3 = 36 | The base 36 hours, subject to calendar fit |
| Twelve repairs | 6 + 12 × 3 = 42 | One available block would give 44 hours |
| Fourteen repairs in a separate surge scenario | 6 + 14 × 3 = 48 | Two blocks would give 52 hours, if that demand and provision became relevant |

The resource holder and customer-facing coordinator examine the actual windows and shared assignments through OPS.13 and [OPS.19](OPERATIONS-MANAGEMENT-PRINCIPLES-FRAMEWORK.md#ops19---reconcile-simultaneous-operating-work-across-cases-and-scales). Assume they establish the necessary calendar fit and qualification for the one-block arrangement. A forecast or suitable skill alone would not assign the technician. They keep the two-block surge request separate; the ambition does not justify buying it automatically.
